title: River-valley civilisations
examples: Why did people settle near rivers?
What was the first writing system?

explain.say: Today we learn about river-valley civilisations. These early societies grew up near big rivers.
Mesopotamia means the land between two rivers. The Tigris and Euphrates rivers were very important there.
Farming was key to these early settlements. People learned to grow crops like barley and wheat.
The need to keep track of crops led to writing. Sumerians developed one of the first writing systems.
These river valleys supported large, complex societies. People built cities and organized governments.
In real life, we still rely on rivers for farming. Modern irrigation systems help us grow food today.

faq.q: Why did civilisations start near rivers?
faq.a: Rivers provided water for drinking and for growing crops. They also allowed for easy travel and trade between settlements.
asks: Why were rivers important for early people?
What did rivers give to early societies?

faq.q: What was the first writing system?
faq.a: The Sumerians developed cuneiform writing. They used wedge-shaped marks pressed into wet clay tablets.
asks: What did the Sumerians write with?

faq.a: Farming allowed people to settle in one place permanently. This led to the creation of villages and eventually large cities.
asks: What was the big change from hunting to farming?

faq.q: Were all river valleys the same?
faq.a: No, different regions had different crops and unique cultural developments. Mesopotamia focused on the Tigris and Euphrates.
asks: Did every river valley develop the same way?
What made one river valley different from another?

faq.a: No, early writing recorded things like trade goods, laws, and amounts of grain. It was used for daily organisation.
asks: What else was writing used for besides stories?
Can writing only record big events?

facts: Mesopotamia means the land between two rivers.
The Tigris and Euphrates rivers were vital to Mesopotamian life.
Early farming allowed settled communities to develop.
Cuneiform was an early writing system used in Mesopotamia.

quiz.say: Early civilisations needed rivers mainly for:
quiz.why: Rivers provided the essential water source needed for both survival and growing food.

wrong.0: Rivers were sources of life, not just military pathways.
wrong.2: While boats were useful, the primary need was for sustenance, which came from the water itself.
wrong.3: Trade was important, but it depended on the initial stability provided by the water source.

quiz.say: The writing system developed in Mesopotamia was called:
quiz.why: The Sumerians are credited with developing this unique wedge-shaped script on clay.

wrong.1: Hieroglyphics are associated with a different ancient civilisation.
wrong.2: This was a later development, not the first system used.
wrong.3: While early writing used pictures, cuneiform was the specific developed form.

quiz.say: Which activity was most directly linked to the development of writing?
quiz.why: Tracking surpluses from farming required a reliable system for record-keeping, which became writing.

wrong.0: While wars happened, the earliest records focused on economic stability.
wrong.1: Mapping was important, but the initial records were about quantifiable goods.
wrong.3: Stories came later; the initial need was practical record keeping.
